tierWindow.goal: Put the three factors of excelling into action: respond to a setback with a growth mindset, sustain motivation and self-belief on a demanding task, and set goals that move your learning forward.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application, selection and comparison (apply, use, choose and distinguish), beyond recognising what the ideas mean.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Realistic study situations with a choice to make; two settled distinctions applied in context, such as fixed versus growth responses and mastery versus performance goals.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding; worked examples model the move, then the learner selects or adapts a response; feedback explains why a choice works.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows what success and excelling mean and that mindset, motivation and goals matter; the introductory course built that. They are now partway through their studies and ready to put these into practice. Teach from application, not first principles: the aim is to use the ideas on real study tasks, not to define them again.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, putting a growth mindset to work: applying it when something goes wrong. Second, motivation and self-belief that last: keeping going on a demanding task. Third, setting goals that move you forward. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about progressing at university: turning what you know about mindset, motivation and goals into things you actually do. By the end you will be able to apply a growth mindset to a setback, use self-belief and the right kind of motivation on a demanding task, and set goals that move your learning forward.

You are past the start of your studies now. The question is no longer what success means, but how to keep making progress when the work gets harder. That is what these three habits are for.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: apply a growth mindset to a setback, use self-efficacy and learning motivation on a demanding task, set mastery goals.

practiceConnection.academic: Progressing at university is built on these three habits working together. Every demanding module, every mark that disappoints, every stretch of work that feels too hard, is a place to apply a growth mindset, draw on self-belief and set a goal that pulls you forward. Build these now and they carry you through the rest of your degree.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced course in this pathway takes these habits into self-regulated learning and the graduate capital you build across your whole degree. Going wider: the same habits underpin Academic Writing, Reflective Practice and Understanding Learning, Assessment and Feedback, where you put them to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Progressing at university is no longer about knowing that mindset, motivation and goals matter; it is about using them. You can apply a growth mindset to a setback, reading a poor result as information rather than a verdict. You can build self-efficacy and draw on learning motivation to keep going on a demanding task. And you can set mastery goals that move your learning forward. Look back at the confidence check to see how far you have moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, these three habits are things you practise in every module. Each setback you meet with a growth response, each demanding task you sustain through self-belief, each mastery goal you set, is progress you are driving yourself. This is also what study and professional life reward: the capacity to keep going and keep developing when the work is hard.
